Rashi on Nedarim 21a:1:1.hebrew: שניהם רוצין בשלשה דינרין - כלומר, זה הנשבע שאינו פוחת לו מן הסלע, לא היה פיו ולבו שוין לכך שלא יפחות לו מן הסלע כלום, אלא להכי נדר כן לזרז את חבירו שיתן לו ג' דינרין — הוא רוצה לבא; וזה שנשבע שלא ליתן לו יותר משקל, לא היה פיו ולבו שוין, שלא היה בדעתו שלא יתן יותר, אלא לכך נדר שיתן לו בג' דינרין. ולפיכך מותרין:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:1:1.english: Both want [it] for three dinars - That is to say, this one who swears that he will not reduce [the price] for him from a sela, his mouth and his heart were not in agreement that he would not reduce anything from the sela for him; rather, he vowed thus in order to urge his fellow to give him three dinars — [for that is what] he wants to arrive at. And this one who swore not to give him more than a shekel, his mouth and his heart were not in agreement, for it was not in his mind that he would not give more; rather, he vowed thus so that he would give [it] to him for three dinars. And therefore they are permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:2:1.english: Who taught - [the four vows that] the Sages dissolved.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:2:2.hebrew: ר' יהודה היא דאמר אין אחד מהן נזיר - דלא סמכא דעתייהו ממש לשם נזירות, אלא תלו נזירותן בזה שבא כנגדן, ולא היה פיו ולבו שוין, להכי אין אחד מהם נזיר. ה"נ לא סמכא דעתייהו בשעת הנדר, דכל חד וחד אדעתא דחבריה כדי לזרזו, ולא הי' פיו ולבו שוים להכי. דאי רבנן דפליגי עליה דר' יהודה — דאמרי אע"ג דלא סמכא דעתייהו להיות נודר ממש בנזיר, דתלה נזירות באחר, הוי נזיר אותו שנתקיימו דבריו — ה"נ, אף על גב דלא סמכא דעתייהו אדבור פיהן, שלא נתכוונו אלא לזרז, אסורים; דאמרינן כשנדרו ודאי סמכא דעתייהו, דזה לא יפחות מסלע וזה לא יוסיף על שקל, והרי פיהן ולבן שוים, ואסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:2:2.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, who said neither of them is a nazirite - Because they did not truly intend [to take on] naziriteship, rather they made their naziriteship dependent on the one coming toward them, and their mouths and hearts were not in agreement; therefore, neither of them is a nazirite. Here too, they did not truly intend [the vow] at the time of the vow, for each one [vowed] based on the intent of his fellow in order to urge him on, and their mouths and hearts were not in agreement for this [vow]. For if [it followed] the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda — who say that even though they did not truly intend to actually vow as a nazirite, since he made naziriteship dependent on another [matter], the one whose words were fulfilled becomes a nazirite — here too, even though they did not truly intend the words of their mouths, as they intended only to urge [each other] on, they are prohibited; since we would say that when they vowed they certainly intended that this one would not take less than a sela and this one would not pay more than a shekel, and thus their mouths and hearts are in agreement, and it is prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:1.hebrew: רבא אמר אפי' תימא רבנן - דפליגי עליה דר' יהודה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:1.english: Rava said: You can even say [it follows] the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:2.hebrew: מי קתני שניהן רצו - דאי קתני הכי, הוה משמע שניהן רצו בתחלה בשלשה דינרין, ואלא עכשיו בשעת הנדר אין רוצין, אלא סמכא דעתייהו אדבור פיהן, ופיהן ולבן שוים, ונדר מעליא הוי:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:2.english: Does it teach: Both wanted - For if it taught thus, it would imply [that] both wanted [it] at the outset for three dinars, whereas now, at the time of the vow, they do not want [it]; rather, their minds rely upon the utterance of their mouth, and their mouth and their heart are in agreement, and it is a valid vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:3.hebrew: רוצין תנן - דמשמע מעיקרא היו רוצין בג' דינרין, ואכתי שניהן נמי רוצין, ולא היה פיהן ולבן שוין. הלכך, אפילו רבנן מודו דמותרין, וכדי לזרז זה את זה נתכוונו שניהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:3:3.english: We learned: [Both] want - Which implies [that] from the outset they wanted three dinars, and still both also want [it], and their mouths and their hearts were not in agreement. Therefore, even the Rabbis agree that they are permitted, and both intended [it only] in order to urge one another on.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:4:1.hebrew: אמר לו טפי מסלע והלה אומר בציר משקל - היכא דאמר שאינו פוחת מסלע וזה אומר שאינו מוסיף על שקל, כיון דדברי שניהם קרובין לשלשה דינרין, אמרינן דנדרי זרוזין הוו. אבל הכא, כיון דאמר טפי מסלע, דהיינו פרוטה, והלה אומר קונם שאיני מוסיף לך על פרוטה פחות משקל, דהשתא מרחקי מילתייהו משלשה דינרין — כיון דדייקי הכי, נדרא הוי ואסורים, או לא, דזירוזין הוה:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:4:1.english: [If he] said to him, "More than a sela," and the other says, "Less than a shekel" - Where [the seller] said that he will not go below a sela and this [buyer] says that he will not add above a shekel, since the words of both of them are close to three dinars, we say that they are vows of encouragement. However, here, since he said "more than a sela," which means [by at least] a perutah, and the other says, "Konam that I will not add for you [even] a perutah [above] less than a shekel," so that now their statements are distanced from three dinars — since they are so exact like this, is it a [binding] vow and they are forbidden [from compromising], or not, [and] it is [a vow of] encouragement?

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:1.english: [He] was importuning - That he was urging him to eat a little with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:2.english: Konam your house, that I will [not] enter - That he vowed that he would not enter his house.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:3.english: And a drop of cold [water] that I taste - [Meaning] not to eat anything with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:4.english: It is permitted to enter his house, and to eat a little, and to drink a drop of cold [water] from him - But not a large meal.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:5.hebrew: שלא נתכוון זה - המסרב, אלא לשום אכילה מרובה, שיסעוד אצלו הרבה; ולשון "טיפת צונן" לא נתכוון זה, שהיא שתיה מועטת:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:5:5.english: This [person] did not intend - [that is,] the one refusing — except for the purpose of a substantial meal, that he would dine with him extensively; and [as for] the expression "a drop of cold [water]," this [person] did not intend [it literally], as it is minimal drinking.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:6:1.english: But he said: A drop of cold [water] - Which implies a small [amount of] drinking and a small [amount of] eating.

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:6:2.hebrew: אלא משתעי איניש הכי - דכי אמר (טיפת צונן) יאכל עמו, ודאי לאכילה מתכוון. וכי נדר זה שאינו טועם עמו טיפת צונן, ודאי לאכילה מרובה נתכוון, ולהכי מותר לשתות טיפת צונן:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:6:2.english: Rather, a person speaks this way - For when [one] says (a drop of cold [water]) [that] he should eat with him, he certainly intends [an actual] meal. And when this one vows that he will not taste a drop of cold [water] with him, he certainly intended a substantial meal, and therefore it is permitted [for him] to drink a drop of cold [water].

Rashi on Nedarim 21a:6:3.hebrew: ה"נ משתעי איניש הכי - דכי נתכוון ליתן שלשה דינרין, אומר שאינו מוסיף על פרוטה פחות משקל. ולעולם נדרי זירוזין הוו, ואפילו דאמר טפי מסלע ובציר משקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 21a:6:3.english: Here too, a person speaks this way - For when he intended to give three dinars, he says that he will not add less than a shekel onto a perutah. Nevertheless, they are vows of motivation, even though he said "more than a sela and less than a shekel."

Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:2:1.hebrew: אלא להפלאה - וא"ת: והא גבי נדרים לא כתב "יפליא"? וי"ל, דילפינן מהדדי, משום דאתק' נדרים לנזירות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:2:1.english: Only by explicitness - And if you ask: But regarding vows, [Scripture] does not write "yafli" [explicitly uttering]? One can answer that we derive [one] from the other, because vows are compared [in Scripture] to naziriteship:

Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:2:2.hebrew: מספיקא לא משעבד נפשיה - וה"נ במתניתין, אע"ג דבשעת הנדר לא היה דעת זה וזה בג' דינרין, אלא הוה דעתיה להוריד כמה שיוכל לזה, דלמא בשעת הנדר מספקא ליה אם חל נדר אם לאו — דשמא יתן לו סלע או יתן לו בב' דינרין — מספיקא לא משעבד נפשיה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:2:2.english: Out of doubt, he does not obligate himself - And so too in our Mishnah: even though at the time of the vow, the intent of both this one and that one was not [set] on three dinars, rather his intent was to bring this one down [in price] as much as he could, [nonetheless,] perhaps at the time of the vow he is in doubt whether [the] vow takes effect or not — for perhaps he will give him a sela or he will give [it] to him for two dinars — out of doubt, he does not obligate himself.

Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:3:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - לא היו מסופקין, אפי' תימא רבנן: מי קתני "שניהן רצו", דהוה משמע רצו לבסוף ולא מתחלה? "רוצים" קתני, משמע דמתחלה כשנודרים היו רוצים בג' אלו שהיו, ואנן סהדי דדעתן לכך, הלכך לאו נדר הוא כלל. דדוקא כשאמר המוכר לבסוף שכך היה דעתו מתחלה, כדפרישית; אבל אם אמר שדעתו למה שהיו אומרים, מכוונת לבם לכך — התם אין נדרי זירוזין, דהוי נדר קיים, ודלא כרבי יהודה משום רבי טרפון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 21a:3:1.english: Rava said - They were not in doubt; you can even say [the Mishnah follows] the Rabbis: does it teach "both wanted," which would imply they wanted [that price] at the end and not from the beginning? It teaches "[both] want," implying that from the beginning when they vow they wanted these three [dinars] that were [agreed upon], and we are witnesses [that] their intention was for this; therefore, it is not a vow at all. For [this applies] specifically when the seller said at the end that such was his intention from the beginning, as I have explained; but if he said that his intention was for what they were saying — [meaning] their hearts were directed to that [price] — there, it is not [a case of] vows of encouragement, for it is a binding vow, and [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Tarfon.
